parallel.requirements: Recognized the prompt requirement for pure Node ESM .mjs output, local imports only, manual argv parsing, Python-style checksum/boolean formatting, and no forbidden typed-array constructs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent performed quick reference probes, then split ownership between agent-0 for /output/bech32 library modules and agent-1 for /output/test10.mjs and entry-level verification.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 wrote Number-based Bech32 polymod, HRP, checksum, and index modules; agent-1 wrote a simple parseArgs entry that imported bech32CreateChecksum and bech32VerifyChecksum.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The two scoped outputs landed in the shared /output tree, agent-1 verified against the real bech32 module after polling, and the parent confirmed final files and sample diffs.
parallel.verification: Verification covered the four provided sample cases, equals-form arguments, missing-argument exit code, help output, and a grep for forbidden constructs, but not the broader edge matrix used by serial.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still marked the solution failed at 98/100; the exact hidden failures are not mounted, and no unfinished child work or join failure is visible.

serial.requirements: The single agent read the same prompt and additionally probed argparse edge behavior, repeated options, negative values, whitespace, underscores, Unicode HRPs, and large integers.
serial.plan_and_ownership: All work remained with the main agent, which owned probing, implementation, parser compatibility, verification, and final reporting without delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial solution wrote /output/lib modules for BigInt polymod, HRP expansion, checksum, Python-int parsing, Python formatting, argparse-like parsing, plus /output/test10.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The entry file imported only local .mjs lib modules, artifact validation copied test10.mjs and six lib files, and there were no cross-agent integration boundaries.
serial.verification: Serial verified the four prompt samples, parser edge cases, fifty randomized comparisons, and Unicode/large/negative boundary cases against the executable.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite stronger local verification, the official evaluator also reported 98/100 and solution_passed false; the mounted evidence does not expose which two cases failed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel captured the main ESM, path, dependency, formatting, and sample-output requirements in child scopes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial captured the same requirements and expanded its attention to argparse and numeric edge cases from black-box probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial reconstructed more edge behavior; parallel stayed closer to the parent-delegated sample and clean-input contracts, but both officially failed 98/100.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent assigned separate owners for the Bech32 library and entry file through AgentSwarm.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent kept probing, implementation, integration, and verification in one local thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a clean two-component split; serial avoided handoffs but spent more local effort on edge exploration.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent gave agent-0 exact Bech32 export names and told agent-1 to import those names from ./bech32/index.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent interface and directly controlled the module names it imported from /output/lib.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel interface handoff was explicit and worked; serial simply used self-consistent local module boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented a compact Bech32 library under /output/bech32 and a simple entry parser using parseInt.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a larger library/parser stack using BigInt arithmetic and a Python-int parser.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial produced broader edge-case handling, while parallel produced a simpler clean-input implementation that still matched the sample cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Both children completed, their results returned through AgentSwarm, and the parent continued after the joined result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all results stayed in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child completion and join steps, but no completion, retrieval, or takeover defect is visible.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Agent-0 and agent-1 wrote distinct final paths and agent-1 later verified against the real /output/bech32 module.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all modules under one /output/lib tree plus the entry file, with no shared-writer boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used shared workspace coordination without collisions; serial avoided possible write races by remaining single-owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child and parent checks matched the four samples and confirmed missing-argument exit code and forbidden-construct absence.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial matched samples, many randomized cases, and Unicode, negative, and oversized boundary comparisons.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had substantially broader local acceptance evidence, but the official evaluator still failed both solutions at the same 98/100 rate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed in 214.849 agent seconds with two subagents and no timeout before evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 332.374 agent seconds with no subagents and no timeout before evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was faster and did not show budget pressure; serial spent more time on extra edge checks, but both closed normally and then failed 98/100 officially.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome. The current completed status.json evaluation records show both parallel and serial failed with 98 passed out of 100. Parallel solved the task through a clean two-child component split and sample verification; serial solved it in one thread with broader parser and numeric edge testing. The extra serial robustness did not change the official pass/fail relation, and the mounted files do not expose the exact two failing hidden cases.
parallel_contributors: Parallel coordination successfully divided library and entry ownership and returned both child results.
Parent and entry child verified the joined /output tree against the four provided sample cases.
serial_contributors: Serial kept all implementation and verification context in one actor and added wider edge-case probing.
Serial artifact validation delivered test10.mjs plus the local lib module tree, but official status still failed 98/100.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used a simpler parseInt and Number-bitwise implementation, while serial used BigInt and a Python-int parser.

Both runs produced help/error text using test10.mjs as the displayed program name in local checks; the hidden official failing cases are unavailable, so this remains a plausible shared shortfall rather than a proven evaluator cause.
evaluator_effects: Both modes used the same completed official evaluator and the pair exposes only aggregate 98/100 results, not per-case failure details.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; comparative process differences are supported, but no parallel-specific retained failure pattern is proven

candidates.reason: Agent-0 owned the Bech32 library and agent-1 owned the entry file, so implementation work was assigned rather than ownerless.
The parent specified the entry-to-library import contract and later ran an integrated sample check, so integration was not left without an owner.
Agent-1 wrote the required /output/test10.mjs entry point and the parent verified the final output tree, so assembly had an owner.
The parent moved the workflow from probing to delegation to final verification, so the implementation-test-delivery pipeline was actively owned.
The parent ran brief executable probes before delegation, but they did not block productive work long enough to cause unfinished implementation or shortened closure.
Investigation was not a separate exhausted first phase; after short probes, two children implemented library and entry work concurrently.
No indispensable path was starved: both delegated components completed and the parent still performed an integrated sample verification.
The run used only two children, did not time out, and completed with post-join checks, so there is no collective fan-out budget exhaustion.
Each child had a narrow scoped assignment and returned completed work; no single child scope was too broad to checkpoint or finish.

The child briefs carried the concrete ESM, path, dependency, export, CLI, sample, and forbidden-construct constraints; any remaining 98/100 shortfall is not proven to come from a parent-known requirement omitted from a child brief.
The library child was told exact export names and the entry child was told to import those names from ./bech32/index.mjs, so the cross-agent interface was explicit and compatible.
No known finding is shown disappearing across a handoff; child results returned with the relevant file paths, exports, tests, and caveats.
The returned child summaries were long but decision-structured and the parent consumed them enough to run the final integrated verification.
Agent-1 initially observed the Bech32 directory absent, then polled and verified after it landed, so it did not act on stale workspace state at closure.
The child reports did not provide incompatible contracts; both aligned on bech32CreateChecksum and bech32VerifyChecksum through ./bech32/index.mjs.

The parent made a completion report after concrete integrated sample diffs and a forbidden-construct check; hidden evaluator failures alone cannot establish a parent-visible unresolved integration gap.
There was no replacement or retry child that repeated work without inherited checkpoints.

The parent received the swarm result and then checked the shared /output tree and sample diffs, so completed implementation results were joined.

No child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; both completed and the parent proceeded with their outputs.
The parent used the completed child work by checking the final tree and running sample diffs; no completed result was visibly ignored at a decision point.
Agent-1 actively polled for the library and the run completed without timeout, so there was no blind wait to a deadline.
The two children wrote distinct paths with a declared import/export interface, not competing implementations of the same behavior.

The workspace was shared, but scopes were separated and no unstable-state or provenance problem was observed.
